sessions.task: idempotent Stripe webhook handler in billing-api

transcript.content: Implement the idempotency fix we designed for the Stripe webhook handler in billing-api: check the Stripe event id against a processed_events table inside the same Postgres transaction as the charge, add the unique index migration, and add tests that replay duplicate events.

Added migration 0042_processed_events with a unique index on stripe_event_id. Updated src/webhooks/stripe.ts so the processed_events insert and the charge insert happen in one Postgres transaction — a duplicate event id now rolls the whole retry back as a no-op.

Added 4 integration tests, including one that replays the exact same webhook payload three times and asserts a single charge. Full suite passes: 142 passed, 0 failed.

Session summary: duplicate webhook retries are now deduplicated at the transaction boundary; nothing is double-charged on retry.

sessions.task: Redis cache layer for the feed endpoint

transcript.content: Add the Redis cache layer to the mobile-backend feed endpoint we discussed: wrap the feed query with a 60s TTL cache and invalidate on new posts and comments.

Created src/feed/cache.ts exposing FeedCache with get-or-compute semantics, wired it into the feed handler, and added invalidation hooks on post-create and comment-create. Kept the Postgres query untouched behind the cache boundary.

Load test at 10x production traffic: p95 latency dropped from 810ms to 90ms with a 97% cache hit rate. All 218 tests pass.

Session summary: the feed endpoint now serves from cache except on the first request per TTL window; feed latency is no longer dominated by the activity join.
